text: Hi Matti, this is your care team. Your CT and biopsy are in five days. Is everything okay for getting there?
Hmm... I have to cancel. There's no bus from Kemi that morning.
I understand. Kela can cover a taxi. Shall I book one for you?
This call doesn't exist in Finland today. Matti would simply not show up. And nobody would know why.
Almost thirty-nine thousand people in Finland are diagnosed with cancer every year.
We know why some of them drop out of care: fear, distance, cost. We know roughly how many. But we don't know who.
It happens between the steps. A referral not booked. A scan cancelled. A missed visit. Almost one in three patients feel their diagnosis came too late.
Part one, today: CareCatalyst for the welfare counties. It watches the pathway signals the county already has, starting with HUS.
When a pathway stalls, the agent calls, asks why, and helps: a new slot, a Kela taxi, a video visit.
Every reason flows back, anonymised. So the county sees where people drop out, right next to the national Goal 3 indicator: treatment within target times.
Today, the institution reaches out to the patient. Tomorrow, it's the other way around. Soon, everyone will have a personal agent.
Meet Eero. Seventy-eight, from Espoo, visually impaired. And this is Jenny.
He bends down to feed her, and his back hurts. Again.
His agent remembers: he saw a doctor for this pain before. Nobody in the system connects those two visits. His agent does.
Eero, your back is hurting again. I think you should get it checked. The centre is in Helsinki, but Kela can cover a taxi. Shall I book tomorrow at eight, before your bingo?
The agent never diagnoses. It only books the check-up, and the ride.
And who does Eero's agent talk to? The county agent we built today. Agent to agent. Eero shares only what's needed, and never has to explain his life again.
Today, we close the gaps the system can see. Tomorrow, the ones only you can see. CareCatalyst. Closing gaps. Connecting care.
